content.text: I've read the full agreement (single section, 75 paragraphs) and searched for audit/inspect/records/verify language — none exists.

input.quote: 5. Fees and Payment. The Parties agree to share any revenue generated as a result of this Agreement, or Customer's use of the Services or the Auction Platform, as set forth and detailed in each applicable Exhibit.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right exercisable by Kubient against the Customer. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verify" return nothing, and the two provisions that could plausibly host such a right — Section 5 (Fees and Payment, a pure revenue-share with payment flowing from Kubient to AP) and Section 6 (Use of Service, which imposes use restrictions but no verification or system-access mechanic) — grant Kubient no examination right. Section 1 requires AP to give "reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation" only for the purpose of Kubient delivering the Services, not for compliance checking, and there is no remote or direct access to AP systems anywhere (no walk-away trigger). The absence of any audit right binding us is better than the preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost), so there is nothing to constrain and no redline is warranted — inserting audit limits would only create a vendor right that does not currently exist. Noted for the record but not flagged: since Impressions are "as measured by Kubient" and revenue flows to us, AP may separately wish to negotiate its own audit right over Kubient's records; that is a customer-favourable addition outside the scope of this rule.
